---
title: "Matrices"
---

::: {.callout-note}

## Learning Outcomes

By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to:

- **Describe** the characteristics of an R matrix, and **explain** its relationship to vectors.
- **Create** new matrices in R.
- **Perform** element-wise operations on matrices, and **explain** how recycling applies to matrix operations.
- **Select and modify** the elements of a matrix.

:::

In R, matrices are a fundamental data structure used to represent two-dimensional collections of homogeneously typed values. Just like vectors, all elements in a matrix must have the same type: one of the [six atomic modes](/tutorials/vectors/atomic_modes.qmd). You can think of R matrices as generalizations of R vectors. Matrices are just vectors with a dimension attribute that tells R to interpret matrices as two-dimensional objects with rows and columns.

That last point is worth sitting with for a moment: everything you already know about vectors — how they're typed, how arithmetic works element-wise, how recycling resolves length mismatches — carries over to matrices almost unchanged. The main new idea in this tutorial is simply *how R keeps track of rows and columns* on top of that
familiar vector foundation.
